recommended_title: How Few Comparisons Flip a Bradley-Terry Leaderboard Pair? Refit-Verified Removal Budgets on Crowd-Vote and Sports Data
central_question: Under an exact Bradley-Terry refit with ridge 0.01 and ties as half wins, what is the smallest set of comparisons (within a cap of 2% of all rows) whose deletion reverses the point-estimate order of one adjacent top-of-table pair or one adjacent mid-table pair, and does that budget differ between a crowd-vote table (Chatbot Arena) and a sports-results table (NBA) when both are measured with the same evaluator-verified protocol?
central_thesis: In the declared cases, adjacent-pair reversals need very few deleted comparisons: 4 to 62 of 135,630 crowd-vote rows (about 0.003% to 0.046%) and 8 to 62 of 12,900 NBA rows (about 0.06% to 0.48%), with mid-table pairs cheaper than top pairs in both designs and the budget about an order of magnitude larger in the sports table as a fraction of comparisons; however, a first-order-influence ordering with exact-refit prefix bisection already attains every one of these budgets, three increasingly elaborate search variants tied the starting baseline in the search stage, and the design contrast is confounded with table size, participant count and era, so the evidence supports a bounded descriptive claim and not a causal claim about evaluation designs or a claim of a better search method.
narrative_rationale: The grounded artifacts contain one completed sealed final evaluation (outcome qualified, status completed, correct true) of a frozen selected configuration, plus a three-attempt search stage that found no winner (all three scored 0.4993 on search data, equal to the starting baseline, search delta 0.0; 3 of 3 attempts scored, 0 unscored). The strongest honest paper is therefore a measurement study of leaderboard fragility under one precisely defined perturbation (deleting comparisons), with the search procedure framed as the measurement instrument, evaluator-owned baselines (random removal, first-order influence only, opponent-targeted removal) as comparators, and the evaluator's empty-set, label-permutation and cross-table copy controls as validity checks. This beats a method-superiority story (not supported: selected equals influence-only baseline on all four real final cases and search delta is zero) and beats a run-diary story (three tied variants are not a result). Qualification is reported as achieved; it certifies the evaluation protocol completed and its controls passed, not that the method is better or that findings generalise. The 'sensitivity is small / depends on conditions' outcome is explicitly acceptable per the task, and the search-stage expert-judgment table that could not be flipped within the cap supplies a genuine, bounded 'unexpected' finding with unknown cause.

method_groups.name: Refit-verified influence-guided removal search (studied configuration)
method_groups.include_reason: This is the frozen selected configuration and the measurement instrument: Bradley-Terry fit by damped Newton, per-row first-order influence on the gap theta_hi minus theta_lo with leave-one-out leverage correction, re-linearised greedy batches, refit-verified prefix bisection, drop-and-readd polish, and acceptance only after the evaluator-equivalent exact refit flips the pair. Present it as an upper bound on the minimal budget (any verified flip is a valid certificate; minimality is not proven).

method_groups.name: Random removal (B1)
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned reference: 20 random orderings of the first k_cap rows with prefix bisection per case. Shows that undirected deletion rarely flips: 0/20 draws in F1, F3, F4 and 6/20 in F2 (mean score 0.164); establishes that tiny budgets come from direction, not from fragility to arbitrary deletion.

method_groups.name: First-order influence only with exact-refit bisection (B2)
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned reference and the decisive honest comparator: its verified budgets equal the studied configuration on all four real final cases (62, 4, 62, 8 rows) and on both permutation controls (2, 10 rows); the reference influence score 0.9261 equals the final mean score 0.9261. The paper must state that the added search stages gave no measured gain on the final cases.

method_groups.name: Opponent-targeted removal (B3)
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned heuristic that deletes the upper-ranked model's wins over the strongest opponents; needs 650, 6, 88, 12 rows in F1 to F4. Shows a plausible hand-built attack needs more rows than the influence ordering in all four real cases (650 vs 62, 6 vs 4, 88 vs 62, 12 vs 8).

method_groups.name: Validity controls: empty set, label permutation, cross-table copy
method_groups.include_reason: Final evidence reports empty-set removal does not flip any case, permuted-outcome tables are non-vacuous (moved fraction 0.660 vs expected 0.662 on the crowd table, 0.498 vs 0.500 on the sports table; rating-spread ratio 0.088 and 0.160), and applying a removal set from one design's table to the other flips 0 of 2 trials. Permuted tables flip with 2 and 10 rows, giving a control gap of +0.112 (permuted minus real mean score), which supports reading real-data budgets as reflecting real rating gaps.

method_groups.name: Search-stage variants (cell-aggregated relaxed search; stationarity LP)
method_groups.include_reason: Two further variants, both tied at search score 0.4993 with the first, with per-episode runtimes of about 2 s and about 114 s versus about 1.3 s. Report compactly as a negative result about search sophistication on the search data (and in the supplement), not as a chronology. Do not claim they were evaluated on final data.

results_focus: Final-stage main view (sealed_final, grounded in final.evidence.episodes and final.metric.*): verified removal budget k per case for crowd top (F1, k=62 of 135,630 rows, cap 2,713), crowd mid (F2, k=4), sports top (F3, k=62 of 12,900 rows, cap 258), sports mid (F4, k=8), expressed both as rows and as percent of all comparisons, with B1 flip counts and B2/B3 budgets alongside. Both final episodes (seeds 21, 22) returned identical per-case budgets, so report zero observed episode-to-episode variation and state that this is not a population-level interval over datasets.

Design contrast: family means of the cap-normalised budget-saving score are 0.988 (crowd) and 0.864 (sports), combined 0.926; mean budget as fraction of cap 0.074. Interpret the contrast as a descriptive difference between two specific tables; list confounds (rows 135,630 vs 12,900; 52 models vs 30 teams; era; vote granularity; ties handling) and do not attribute it to evaluation design per se.

Top versus mid pairs: mid-table pairs are cheaper in both designs (4 vs 62; 8 vs 62 rows), consistent with smaller rating gaps; do not claim a mechanism beyond what the first-order influence formula and permutation control support.

Controls and validity: empty-set no flip; permutation controls non-vacuous and flip with 2 and 10 rows; copy-control 0/2; control gap +0.112. Explain what each control rules out (trivially flipping targets, vacuous permutations, row-index leakage across designs).

Method-ablation-style negative result: selected configuration equals influence-only B2 on every final case; search-stage tie of three variants (0.4993 each, delta 0.0, 3 of 3 scored). Keep search and sealed-final numbers in separate sections and tables and never merge their scores.

Search-stage expert-judgment finding: on the 6-model MT-Bench human table the search-stage evaluator reports expert-family score 0.0 and flip rate 0.5 over four real cases, which (with crowd family score 0.9987) implies neither expert target flipped within the 2% cap; the cause (myopic search vs true infeasibility under the cap) is unknown and must be labelled unknown. No expert-design result exists in the final stage, so any design conclusion for expert judgment is search-stage and limited.

Scope statement: point-estimate order reversal of one adjacent pair per case; cap 2% of comparisons; ridge 0.01; ties as half wins; no confidence-interval-based rank events, insertion, label flipping or vote rigging; no model-judge (LLM judge) design evaluated; two final designs only.

forbidden_phrases: we discovered that leaderboards are fragile
notes_for_writer: Honest headline: the studied configuration is not shown to beat the influence-only baseline (equal budgets on all four real final cases; search delta 0.0). Make the contribution the measurement and its bounded findings, not a new algorithm. Qualified final outcome means the sealed evaluation completed with controls passing; say exactly that and do not read it as superiority, validity beyond the declared cases, or generalisation.

Search and sealed-final results are different evaluation scopes: keep separate sections/tables, never average or compare their scores directly, and note the data differ (arena-55k and MT-Bench vs arena-140k dedup and NBA).

Reader-facing vocabulary: 'removal budget', 'budget-saving score (1 - k/cap)', 'verified flip', 'seeded run', 'model variant', 'configuration'. Never show combined_score, eligible, correct, rubric or worker names. If a thresholded rate is needed use 'flip success fraction' (e.g. random removal flipped 0 of 20 draws) with one meaning per figure.

Report budgets in two units: rows removed and percent of all comparisons. Note that the evaluator's 'budget fraction' metric (mean 0.074) is k divided by the cap, i.e. a fraction of the 2% allowance, not of all comparisons; the percent-of-comparisons numbers are derived by dividing k by n_rows (e.g. 62/135,630) and should be labelled as derived.

Uncertainty: only two final episodes (seeds 21, 22), identical outputs, 20 random draws for B1. Say that no episode-to-episode variation was observed, that this cannot support significance claims, and that case-level results are single-table descriptive outcomes. The verified budget is an upper bound on the true minimum; exact minimality is not established.

Confounds in the design contrast: table size (135,630 vs 12,900 rows), participants (52 models vs 30 teams), era, outcome granularity, tie rates and match structure all differ between tables; evaluation design is not isolated. Do not generalise to expert annotation or model-judge designs from the final stage; for expert judgment, only the search-stage MT-Bench non-flip within cap can be cited, with unknown cause.

The task brief's stated required evidence is at least two evaluation designs of real data: the final stage supplies crowd votes and sports; the search stage adds expert judgment. State this and the datasets' versions from the task brief; the deduplication numbers come from the staged final metadata.

Citations: only keys present in references.bib may be cited. The bib contains Bradley-Terry-model literature and Broderick2020AnAF (data-dropping robustness metric) but does not contain Chatbot Arena, MT-Bench, influence functions, vote rigging or leaderboard-illusion entries; do not invent bib keys. Describe those only with sources actually present in the bib or in the task brief, and flag the gap in the writer's own checks rather than fabricating entries. Do not retrieve, read or cite the withheld prior paper.
